title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent remediation reminders in Teams
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says Teams app availability has no documented automation. Microsoft documents Update-M365TeamsApp for that setting; the roadmap facts, preview behaviour and principal portal routes are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.claim: The roadmap describes administrator visibility into remediation progress through the Data Security Posture Management dashboard.
claims.quote: Its’ closed-loop workflow ensures that remediation progress is tracked and confirmed, giving admins real-time visibility and control via the Data Security Posture Management dashboard.

claims.claim: The remediation function covers SharePoint and OneDrive file alerts.
claims.quote: For Sharepoint/OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs Attention, the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file

claims.claim: Remediation applies to alerts triaged as Needs attention.
claims.quote: This is applicable only for the alerts categorized as "Needs Attention".

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: The agent sends Teams messages to the user who last modified the file.
claims.quote: Reminders are sent once daily to the user who is last modifier of the file in context

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The message asks the user, rather than the agent, to remove sensitive information.
claims.quote: the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file, and ask them to remove the sensitive information found in the file related to the alert. (Preview)

claims.claim: Learn documents remediation reminders as preview and warns that the design can change before general availability.
claims.quote: Remediation reminders for the Data Security Triage Agent are currently in Preview. Features and steps described in this article might change before general availability.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Reminders are sent once daily.
claims.quote: Reminders are sent once daily

claims.claim: A reminder combines up to 10 files when multiple files require remediation.
claims.quote: (combining up to 10 files if multiple files require remediation).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The message includes the file name.
claims.quote: The remediation message includes the file name

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The message describes the sensitive information requiring attention.
claims.quote: a description of what sensitive information requires attention.

claims.claim: A remediated file is removed from the next day's reminder.
claims.quote: Once the last person who modified, remediates the file, the file is removed from the remediation reminder for the next day.

claims.claim: No reminder is sent when there are no files requiring remediation.
claims.quote: If no files are found, no reminder is sent.

claims.claim: Enabling reminders also enables the Teams bot for the tenant.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting also enables the bot in Microsoft Teams for the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Triage Agent alert queue in DLP displays remediation progress, including fully remediated alerts.
claims.quote: You can view remediation status at the alert level on the Triage Agent alert queue in the DLP solution. This view lets a user see fully remediated alerts, meaning users remediated all files implicated in the alert.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In progress indicates outreach occurred but the user has not remediated all files.
claims.quote: In progress means that the Agent reached out to the user, but the user didn't remediate all the files yet.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Error indicates that the Teams message could not be sent.
claims.quote: Error indicates that the Teams message couldn't be sent.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Each alert's Related assets section displays per-file remediation status.
claims.quote: You can see the status inside each DLP alert in the Related assets section that lists all the files implicated in the alert and the respective remediation status.

claims.claim: The cited Learn setup page does not describe the roadmap's DSPM remediation dashboard view.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Data Security Triage Agent DSPM remediation dashboard'; opened the cited DLP agent setup page and searched its full fetched text for dashboard, DSPM and Posture: no matches.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Remediation is admin-opt-in, with reminders off in one-click setup, so no reminders arrive without enabling them.
claims.quote: The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are: ... Remediation reminder: Turned OFF (Preview)

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Both the org-wide Microsoft apps setting and the agent app's availability must permit delivery.
claims.quote: Two settings must be correctly configured for the Data Security Triage Agent to send remediation messages through Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The setup page specifies both per-seat licensing and pay-as-you-go billing, supporting the mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: This agent requires both the standard per seat licensing model and the pay-as-you-go billing model.
claims.fix: Retain the setup page's attribution and mixed model, but append to licensing notes and Cost and licensing: 'The Security Copilot capacity page also documents automatically created inclusion capacity when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/security-compute-units-capacity. This reports the differing capacity treatment rather than presenting purchased capacity as the sole model.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The organisation must be licensed for Microsoft Data Loss Prevention to use the DLP triage agent.
claims.quote: Your organization must be licensed for: Microsoft Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to use the DLP triage agent.

claims.where: front matter: cost; summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The triage agent consumes security compute units for its tasks independently of enabling remediation, supporting variable metered cost.
claims.quote: The agent consumes security compute units (SCUs) as it performs its tasks.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: SCUs must be provisioned for the triage agent to work.
claims.quote: You must have SCUs provisioned for the triage agent to work.

claims.claim: SCU consumption depends on the number and type of alerts processed.
claims.quote: The number of SCUs consumed depends on the number and type of alerts that are processed.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented preview remediation capability costs nothing extra beyond the SCUs needed to triage the alert first.
claims.quote: The Remediation Capability doesn't cost anything extra. The only costs associated with using this capability are the SCUs needed to triage the DLP alert first.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Provisioned Security Copilot capacity is billed by the hour.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Overage Security Copilot capacity is billed on usage.
claims.quote: the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage units can be configured as unlimited or a maximum amount.
claims.quote: Overage units are billed on-demand and can be set as unlimited or a maximum amount.

claims.claim: The agent can be assigned an Agent Identity that allows data access and actions.
claims.quote: The agent is assigned Agent Identity, which allows it to access data and take actions

claims.claim: The agent can instead be set up using the identity of the user setting it up.
claims.quote: or can be set up by assigning the user's identity who is setting the agent.

claims.claim: Purview automatically installs the Teams app for a user when sending that user's remediation message.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview automatically installs the app for a specific user at the time a remediation message is sent.

claims.claim: The app needs to be available rather than preinstalled.
claims.quote: The Data Security Triage Agent app doesn't need to be preinstalled for users. ... The app only needs to be available (not blocked) in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The agent triages active-mode DLP policies, not policies in simulation mode.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode. It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Learn identifies org-wide Microsoft apps enabled but the individual agent app blocked as a common misconfiguration.
claims.quote: A common misconfiguration occurs when the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle is enabled but the Data Security Triage Agent app is individually blocked.

claims.claim: Configuring the Teams settings requires Teams admin permissions.
claims.quote: You must have Teams admin permissions to configure the Microsoft Teams Admin Center settings described in this article.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Purview admin configuring the agent may lack the required Teams admin permissions.
claims.quote: The Purview admin or analyst who configures the triage agent might not have permissions to access the Microsoft Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: The broader triage agent covers Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams alerts.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP triages alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams.

claims.claim: The tenant must be onboarded to Security Copilot.
claims.quote: Your tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 data sharing must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable Microsoft 365 data sharing in Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview plug-in must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable the Microsoft Purview plug-in in Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: There can be only one instance of each agent per tenant.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.claim: The triage agent can be deployed from Microsoft Purview or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals

claims.claim: Management, editing and deactivation are available only in the Purview portal, including after deployment from Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals, but can only be managed, edited, and disabled from the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Deactivating the agent stops alert triage.
claims.quote: Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts.

claims.claim: Deactivating does not remove the agent.
claims.quote: It doesn't remove the agent

claims.claim: Blocking app availability for a user prevents a generated remediation message from being sent to that user.
claims.quote: Blocking the app for a user is a hard block. Even if an alert is triaged and a remediation message is generated, the message won't be sent to users for whom the app is blocked.

claims.claim: The feature's Teams configuration page says setting availability to No one immediately stops all remediation messages.
claims.quote: if you need to immediately stop all remediation messages, set availability to No one.
claims.fix: Keep the feature-specific guidance but append: 'General Teams app-centric management guidance says UI or PowerShell availability changes can take up to 24 hours to apply to all users.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management#migrate-to-app-centric-management, which states 'UI or PowerShell changes take up to 24 hours to apply to all users'. Report the documentation discrepancy rather than promising an unqualified immediate stop.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Remediation policies are always a subset of triage policies.
claims.quote: Policies enabled for remediation are always a subset of policies enabled for triage.

claims.where: controls[0].governs, controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Agent configuration includes remediation reminders and a reminder-duration setting controlling follow-up days.
claims.quote: Select Agent configuration for editing and configuring settings like Trigger, alert timeframe, remediation reminders, reminder duration, and policy scope. ... The reminder duration reports the number of days the Agent should follow up with the user

claims.where: controls[5].governs, controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Usage monitoring reports SCU consumption through the Security Copilot usage monitoring tool rather than itself specifying a spending limit.
claims.quote: Select Usage monitoring. ... You can track your SCU consumption in the usage monitoring tool.

claims.claim: The Purview route to reminder configuration is Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration.
claims.quote: Select Go to agent for agent you want to edit. ... Select Edit agent. ... Select Agent configuration for editing and configuring settings like Trigger, alert timeframe, remediation reminders, reminder duration, and policy scope.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct configuration page but stops before the switch. Set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Remediation reminders in Microsoft Teams'; retain the note about Reminder duration.

claims.claim: Remediation policy scope is under Purview Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Set agent scope > Edit > Select policies > Remediation.
claims.quote: Select Edit agent > Agent configuration. ... Under Set agent scope, select Edit. ... In the Select policies panel, enable the Remediation toggle only for the policies where you want remediation messages sent to users.

claims.claim: App availability is under Teams apps > Manage apps > Data Security Triage Agent > Users and groups > Edit availability in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Search for Data Security Triage Agent and select it. ... Go to the Users and groups tab. ... Select Edit availability.

claims.claim: The Microsoft apps toggle is under Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Actions > Org-wide app settings. ... In the Org-wide app settings panel, set the Microsoft apps toggle to On.

claims.claim: Deactivation is under Purview Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > ellipses (three dots) > Deactivate agent.
claims.quote: Select Explore agents. ... Select Go to agent for the agent you want to deactivate. ... select the ellipses (three dots) that are located next to the Edit agent button. ... Select Deactivate agent.

claims.claim: SCU monitoring is under Purview Agents > Explore agents > View agent > Edit agent > Usage monitoring.
claims.quote: select Agents. ... Select Explore agents. ... Select View agent for agent you want to edit. ... Select Edit agent. ... Select Usage monitoring.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or REST operation is documented for setting remediation reminders or duration.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview triage agent configure remediation reminders deactivate API PowerShell automation' and 'Purview triage remediation API'; opened the DLP agent setup and Teams configuration pages. Results document portal configuration, not an operation setting reminders or duration.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the agent's remediation policy scope.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview DLP triage agent remediation reminders policy scope deactivate usage monitoring PowerShell Graph REST API'; opened the DLP agent setup and Teams configuration pages. No operation setting the agent's remediation policy scope was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for the Teams app's user and group availability.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'powershell', call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/update-m365teamsapp?view=teams-ps', and update the rendered API cell. In the note, identify <app-id> as the Data Security Triage Agent's Teams application ID and explain that Everyone makes the app available to everyone. Replace the broad automation-absence paragraph with: 'No automation operation was found for remediation reminders, remediation policy scope, agent deactivation, SCU usage monitoring or the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle at the time of writing (November 2026). Teams app availability can be changed with Update-M365TeamsApp.'

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft apps org-wide API' and 'Teams org-wide Microsoft apps toggle Set-M365TeamsAppSettings PowerShell API'; opened Graph teamsAppSettings and the Teams configuration page. The Graph properties do not expose this toggle; custom-app cmdlets concern another setting.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for deactivating this DLP triage agent.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview agent deactivate PowerShell' and 'Purview triage agent configure remediation reminders deactivate API PowerShell automation'; opened DLP agent setup. It documents Deactivate agent in Purview; no matching automation operation was found.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for monitoring this agent's SCU consumption.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Security Copilot usage API agent SCU' and 'Security Copilot usage monitoring REST'; opened DLP agent setup, SCU capacity and Manage security compute unit usage. They document dashboard monitoring and export, but no matching usage-monitoring API operation.

claims.claim: Microsoft points readers to Security Copilot pricing pages for SCU pricing.
claims.quote: For more information, see Microsoft Security Copilot pricing and the Pricing calculator page.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to verify infrastructure configuration controls that have no corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Confirm Security Copilot onboarding, Microsoft 365 data sharing and the Microsoft Purview plug-in are in place, and that SCUs are provisioned for the agent ... Monitoring of the agent's SCU consumption
claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout checklist bullet; the infrastructure prerequisites remain documented in Scope. Do not add controls rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends policy scoping for routine remediation control and Teams blocking as another safeguard.
claims.quote: Use policy scoping in Purview for routine control over what files and locations trigger remediation. Use Teams Admin Center blocking as another safeguard

controlChecks.governs: Whether the agent sends remediation reminders in Teams, and the reminder duration
Which DLP policies are enabled for remediation messages
Which users and groups the Data Security Triage Agent Teams app is available to
Whether Microsoft-published apps can be used in the organisation (needed for remediation messages)
Whether the agent keeps triaging alerts
Monitoring of the agent's SCU consumption
